The Stratospheric Particle Injection for Climate Engineering (SPICE) project was a UK research programme (supported by EPSRC, NERC and STFC, with funding on the order of £2 million) to study solar radiation management, including a proposed limited field test of a delivery system sometimes described as a 'hose to the sky' from a balloon. In 2012 the outdoor test was cancelled after controversy, including an open letter from civil-society groups such as the ETC Group calling for suspension pending international agreement, and after governance and patent concerns. Project leadership continued laboratory and modelling elements. A related public-dialogue exercise found that many participants were more willing to allow a small field trial than to endorse actual use of stratospheric aerosols. SPICE was not a secret spraying programme and did not deploy climate-altering amounts of material. Cancellation of a small engineering test is not evidence that a covert global SAI fleet already exists. The episode is often cited in geoengineering-governance literature as an early example of public contestation of outdoor solar-geoengineering research.
